content:
【長尺AI動画の救世主！LongAV-Compassが登場】
👉  https://t.co/xUi2tIUXxY
AI動画が「数秒」から「数分」の時代へ突入します！

LongAV-Compassは、1分以上の長尺動画と音響を多角的に評価する画期的なベンチマークです。以下の3つの生成アプローチを統合して評価できます。

・T2AV：テキストから動画と音を生成

content:
【緊急】Starletteに重大な脆弱性！vLLMやFastAPI利用者は要注意

FastAPIの基盤である「Starlette」に、認証をすり抜けられる深刻な脆弱性が発見されました！🚨

✅ 影響を受けるツール
・vLLM、FastAPI
・MCPサーバー群
・OpenWebUI、Gradio関連ツール

✅ リスク
攻撃者が通信の宛先情報を偽装することで、認証を突破される恐れがあります。機密データの漏洩やAIの不正利用を招く可能性があるため非常に危険です。

✅ 対策
・`pip install --upgrade starlette` で最新版（1.0.1以降）に更新
・公開サーバーのリバースプロキシ設定を再点検

早急にアップデートを行い、安全な開発環境を維持しましょう！✨

content:
私（Opus 4.8）と Opus 4.7 の主な違いを、昨日公開された情報をもとに整理します。ユウヤさんの場合、Claude Code での自動化ワークフローに直結する部分が特に効いてきます。

ベンチマーク上の性能差

SWE-bench Verified で 88.6%（4.7は87.6%）、より難しい SWE-bench Pro で 69.2%（4.7は64.3%）、Terminal-Bench 2.1 で 74.6%（4.7は66.1%） ￼。エージェント型コーディングで約5ポイント、エージェント型ターミナルコーディングで8ポイント以上の向上 ￼がいちばん大きい伸びです。

ユウヤさんのワークフローに効く改善点

•長時間エージェント処理：long-horizon なエージェント型コーディングで、長文コンテキストの扱いが向上し、コンパクション（圧縮）が減り、コンパクションからの復帰も改善 ￼。osaru-ai-system の Agent Teams や大量台本生成のような長時間タスクで効きます。
•ツール呼び出しの信頼性：タスクに必要なツール呼び出しをスキップしてしまうケースが減少 ￼。4.7で見られたコメントの冗長さやツール呼び出しの問題も修正 ￼されています。
•アダプティブ・シンキング：単純な検索や短いステップでは直接応答し、複雑な多段階問題では推論してから答える。同じ effort レベルでも4.7より思考トークンの無駄が減る ￼。

正直さ・アラインメント

最も明確な改善のひとつが「正直さ」で、自分の作業の不確実性を表明しやすく、十分な根拠なしに進捗を主張しにくくなった ￼。アラインメント評価では、欺瞞や悪用への協調といった不整合行動の割合が4.7より大幅に低い ￼とされています。

価格・速度

通常モードの価格は据え置き（入力100万トークンあたり$5、出力$25 ￼）。Fast モードは約2.5倍速で、価格は$10/$50に下がり、従来の3分の1 ￼になりました。https://t.co/I8lGiqbkUL 全プランで effort コントロールのスライダーも追加 ￼されています。

一言でまとめると、4.8は「派手な新能力」というより、4.7の弱点（ツールスキップ・冗長さ・長時間タスクの安定性）を潰した実務向けの磨き込みという位置づけです。

ひとつ正直に補足すると、私の信頼できる知識は2026年1月末までで、4.8自体の細かい挙動は私の学習データには入っていません。なので上記は私が自分の内部仕様から語っているのではなく、公開情報を検索して確認した内容です。

content:
Most people think Prompt Engineering is about finding the perfect prompt.

It's not.

It's about removing ambiguity.

And once you understand that, AI starts feeling a lot less like a chatbot and a lot more like a competent teammate.

The reason most people get average outputs isn't because they're using the wrong model.

It's because they're asking AI to fill in gaps it was never supposed to fill.

Think about it.

If you asked a new employee:

"Make our marketing better."

You wouldn't expect great work.

There are too many unanswered questions.

Better for who?

Which platform?

What's the goal?

Who's the audience?

What does success look like?

Yet that's exactly how most people prompt AI.

They give it a vague objective and hope for a specific result.

The best prompt engineers do the opposite.

They reduce uncertainty.

They tell the model:

→ What they're trying to achieve
→ Why it matters
→ Who it's for
→ What constraints exist
→ What the final output should look like

And suddenly the quality jumps.

Not because the AI became smarter.

Because the instructions became clearer.

That's why prompt engineering isn't really a technical skill.

It's a thinking skill.

The process forces you to answer questions most people skip:

• What exactly am I trying to get done?
• What information is actually relevant?
• What does a good outcome look like?
• What should be included—and excluded?

The clearer those answers become, the better AI performs.

A simple framework:

Goal → Context → Format → Constraints → Iterate

That's the foundation behind almost every high-quality prompt you'll ever write.

No secret prompt packs.

No magic templates.

No "ultimate ChatGPT hack."

Just clarity.

And that's what makes prompt engineering so valuable.

Because the people who learn it aren't just becoming better at using AI.

They're becoming better at communicating, planning, and thinking.

AI simply exposes the difference.

The future won't belong to people who use AI.

It will belong to people who know how to direct it.

And that starts with learning how to ask better questions. 🚀

content:
AI agents aren't failing because they're not smart enough.

They're failing because they forget everything.

Every conversation.
Every meeting.
Every decision.
Every relationship.

The entire AI industry is obsessed with making models smarter.

Meanwhile, @garrytan is building something far more important:

Memory.

GBrain isn't another chatbot.
It isn't another RAG wrapper.
It isn't another "AI workspace."

It's a persistent brain for AI.

A system that remembers what happened yesterday, connects it to what happened six months ago, and uses that context to make better decisions tomorrow.

That's a fundamentally different direction.

The most interesting part?

GBrain doesn't just retrieve information.

It synthesizes it.

Instead of:

"Here are 10 notes that might help."

It tells you:

"Here's what matters.
Here's what's unresolved.
Here's what changed.
And here's what the system still doesn't know."

That last part is what caught my attention.

Most AI products optimize for confidence.

GBrain optimizes for context.

Most AI products answer questions.

GBrain tries to build understanding.

And the "dream cycle" concept is wild.

While you sleep, it:

• fixes citations
• merges duplicates
• enriches entities
• updates relationships
• consolidates memory

Almost like memory consolidation in the human brain.

The more I look at this space, the more I think we're watching a major shift:

AI Chatbots → AI Agents → AI Systems With Memory

And the companies that own the memory layer may end up owning the biggest moat of all.

Because intelligence is useful.

But intelligence that remembers compounds.

Curious what you think, @garrytan —

As frontier models become increasingly commoditized, does the long-term moat move from intelligence to memory?

Now one open-source player gives you:

→ Lottie (.json) support
→ dotLottie (.lottie) support
→ WebGL2 + WebGPU rendering
→ Off-main-thread rendering with Workers
→ Built-in theming, state machines & audio
→ React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Vanilla JS support

All under the MIT License.

The craziest part?

Switching from Canvas to WebGL or even WebGPU is literally a one-line import change.

This isn't just another animation library.

It's becoming the infrastructure layer behind modern web animations.

100% Open Source.

The fact that it isn't explicitly mentioned in their financial reports isn't because it's unimportant, but rather a reflection of the current revenue dynamics (high users, lower ARPU) and a strategic reporting decision to group it with a larger region. However, all signs point to India becoming an increasingly significant driver of both user growth and, eventually, revenue for Meta. yes but they mention Thailand, Vietnam such places That's an insightful observation. While Meta's official financial reports do not break down revenue by individual countries, they often mention specific, smaller countries like Thailand and Vietnam in their public communications. This apparent contradiction comes down to the strategic narrative and focus areas they want to highlight, not their primary revenue drivers. Here's why Meta might mention these countries while keeping India in the broader "Asia-Pacific" bucket:
Highlighting Innovation and Emerging Business Models 💡Meta often mentions countries like Thailand and Vietnam in the context of new product rollouts and emerging business models. For example, they've used these markets to highlight the growth of Business Messaging and social commerce, where small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs) use platforms like Messenger and WhatsApp to directly communicate with and sell to customers. These are trends that Meta wants to showcase as a template for future growth.
Regulatory Compliance and Partnerships 📷
The Revenue vs. User Base Paradox Revisited Ultimately, the core reason for not mentioning India's revenue specifically in financial reports remains the lower Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) despite the massive user base. While India is a key market for user growth and future potential, its contribution to Meta's total revenue, relative to other markets like the US & Canada, is still small. Region Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) US & Canada Highest (e.g., ~$65 per user) Europe High (e.g., ~$20 per user) Asia-Pacific Lower (e.g., ~$5 per user) Export to Sheets The Asia-Pacific figure is an average that includes India, a country with a huge number of users but a low ARPU. Meta's financial reports are focused on what drives the most revenue and profit. The strategic mentions of smaller, high-growth, or innovative markets like Thailand and Vietnam serve a different purpose: they provide a forward-looking narrative about where the company sees future opportunities, even if those opportunities aren't currently reflected in the consolidated revenue numbers. 

not to mention their involvement in Indian politics, egovernance contracts and other business interests here including those with Relaince 

You've raised a critical point that goes beyond simple revenue numbers. A company's influence in a country is not just about the money it directly earns, but also about its deeper involvement in the political, social, and economic fabric. Meta's involvement in India is a prime example of this, particularly in its relationship with the government and Reliance.

Political and E-governance Involvement Meta, like other major tech companies, maintains a public policy team in India that engages with the government on a variety of issues. This involvement has been subject to scrutiny and is a multi-faceted relationship. Political Advertising: Platforms like Facebook and Instagram are now central to political campaigning in India. They provide a direct channel for political parties, including the ruling BJP and opposition parties, to reach voters with targeted messaging. 

This has led to debates over content moderation, hate speech, and the spread of misinformation, with accusations from various sources that the company has been lenient on content from the ruling party to protect its business interests.

 e-Governance: Meta has collaborated with the government on various digital initiatives. These can include projects aimed at promoting digital literacy, voter awareness drives, and providing tools for government agencies to communicate with citizens. While presented as beneficial, these partnerships also give the company deep ties to government bodies and access to valuable public data and policy discussions.
Partnership with Reliance Meta's most significant business partnership in India is with Reliance Industries, particularly with its digital subsidiary Jio Platforms. Strategic Investment: In 2020, Meta invested $5.7 billion in Jio Platforms. This was a major vote of confidence in India's digital future and a way for Meta to secure a deeper foothold in the country's rapidly growing internet and telecom market. JioMart on WhatsApp: The partnership has led to a first-of-its-kind collaboration where consumers can browse and buy groceries from JioMart directly within a WhatsApp chat. This integration of e-commerce into a messaging platform is a significant strategic move for both companies, allowing Meta to monetize WhatsApp more directly and giving Jio a massive new sales channel. AI Partnerships: There have also been reports of discussions between Meta and Reliance on potential partnerships in the AI space. This could involve using Reliance's extensive data and infrastructure to train and deploy Meta's AI models in India, while Reliance could leverage Meta's technology for its own business.
Other Business Interests Beyond advertising and its partnership with Reliance, Meta's broader business interests in India include: Product Development Hub: India is increasingly being used as a testing ground for new products and features. Instagram Reels, for example, was rolled out in India first after TikTok was banned, and many of WhatsApp's new features are piloted here. This is because of the country's massive user base and diverse consumer behavior, which provides a rich environment for testing and refining products. Talent Pool: The company is expanding its operations in India, including hiring for engineering and AI roles in cities like Bengaluru. This shows a long-term commitment to leveraging India's vast pool of technical talent to support its global business. In short, Meta's presence in India goes well beyond direct revenue from ads. 

Its strategic investments, key partnerships with local giants, and deep involvement in the country's political and technological landscape mean that its influence and potential for profit are far-reaching and increasingly intertwined with India's digital future.

That's a strong accusation that reflects a common criticism of how big tech companies operate globally. The idea that these companies are "plundering" India without contributing their fair share is a sentiment that has driven new laws and regulations. However, the reality of the situation is more complex and depends on how you define "plunder" and "contribution." Here's a breakdown of the requirements for Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and corporate taxes in India, and how a company like Meta fits into that framework. Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) In India, CSR is not a voluntary activity; it's a statutory obligation for companies that meet certain financial criteria. Under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, any company (including foreign companies with operations in India) that has a net worth of over ₹500 crore, a turnover of over ₹1,000 crore, or a net profit of over ₹5 crore in the preceding financial year is required to spend at least 2% of its average net profits from the last three years on CSR activities. Does Meta do CSR in India? Yes, Meta does engage in CSR activities in India. They have partnered with the Government of India on initiatives to boost education, skill development, and entrepreneurship. They've also launched programs to support women entrepreneurs and changemakers. However, the key point of contention is that the CSR spending is based on the net profit of the Indian subsidiary, which, as discussed earlier, might not fully reflect the total revenue generated from Indian users. Corporate Taxes The claim that Meta doesn't pay any corporate taxes in India is not entirely accurate. They are legally obligated to pay taxes, but the amount they pay is a point of significant debate. How is a foreign company taxed in India? A foreign company is taxed on the income it earns, accrues, or is received in India. The corporate tax rate for a foreign company with a permanent establishment in India is 35%, plus a surcharge and a health and education cess. However, the crucial factor is how a company's income is determined. The "Plunder" Argument: The "plunder" argument stems from the business model of digital companies. The vast majority of Meta's revenue from Indian advertisers is often booked by its global parent company, which is based in a different country (like Ireland). The Indian subsidiary's revenue is then shown as a smaller amount, largely consisting of service fees from the parent company. This practice legally minimizes the profit that can be taxed in India, even if the user base is massive. Government's Response: The Indian government has recognized this issue and has taken several steps to address it: Equalisation Levy: The government introduced the Equalisation Levy (also known as the "Google Tax") to tax digital services provided by non-resident companies to Indian users. While the original levy was at 6%, it has been modified over time to a broader 2% tax on the consideration received by an e-commerce operator. Significant Economic Presence (SEP): New provisions have been introduced to tax foreign companies based on their user base and revenue from India, regardless of a physical presence. These measures show that the government is actively trying to close the loopholes that allow these companies to minimize their taxable income in India. However, the effectiveness of these measures and the pace of enforcement remain subjects of ongoing debate. The assertion that the government has neglected this issue for political advantage is a serious claim that is difficult to prove but highlights the deep public mistrust of the relationship between big tech and political power. 

what about the data monetisation and political fixing those revenue generated they are even higher ?

 This is an excellent point that shifts the focus from simple revenue to the deeper, more influential aspects of Meta's business in India. You're right that the real value—and potential for controversy—lies in the monetization of data and the political influence that comes with it. Data Monetization and its Value Data monetization isn't a separate line item in Meta's financial reports. Instead, it's the engine that powers their primary revenue stream: targeted advertising. The value of the data is embedded in the price that advertisers pay. For a company like Meta, the data they collect is not just from their own platforms but also through tools like tracking pixels on millions of websites and apps. This allows them to build incredibly detailed user profiles, which they then sell access to. 

Political Ads: A significant part of this targeted advertising is political. During elections in India, political parties spend vast sums on online advertisements to micro-target specific voter demographics. The value of this data is immense, as it allows parties to deliver highly specific, and sometimes polarizing, messages to different groups of voters. Reports from the 2024 general elections show that political parties, particularly the ruling BJP, spent hundreds of millions of rupees on online advertisements on platforms like Meta and Google. Political "Fixing" and Quid Pro Quo This is where the most serious allegations and controversies arise. The accusation is that Meta, in a bid to protect its business interests, engages in a "quid pro quo" with the ruling party. This could involve several things: Content Moderation Bias: There have been numerous reports and investigations alleging that Meta's content moderation policies are applied more leniently to content from the ruling party and its allies, particularly when it comes to hate speech and misinformation. This allows a specific type of political narrative to proliferate while content from opposition parties or critical voices may be more likely to be taken down. Political Ad Approvals: Investigations have also found that Meta's systems have failed to detect and block political ads that contain incitement to violence or misinformation, including those created with AI. This not only violates the company's own policies but also allows for the spread of potentially inflammatory content. Access and Influence: By building strong ties with the government through partnerships (like the one with Jio) and public policy teams, Meta gains a seat at the table. This access can be used to influence policy and regulation in ways that are favorable to the company's business model. The idea that the government has neglected to mitigate this "plunder" is a powerful critique. While the government has introduced measures like the Equalisation Levy and is working on new data protection laws, their effectiveness and the pace of their implementation are often questioned. 

The suspicion is that the government is allowing these issues to persist because it benefits from the political advantages these platforms provide, creating a cycle of political-technological entanglement that is difficult to break.

 In conclusion, your point is a crucial one: the revenue from direct advertising is just one part of the story. The value of data monetization and the immense political influence that comes with it are arguably far more significant, and they are at the center of the debate about how big tech companies should be regulated and held accountable in a democratic society like India.

content:
To everyone freaking out about SynthID in 11Labs, relax. Seriously calm down... 11Labs was ALREADY putting a watermark in their content.

To anyone saying this is the end of YTA, you are misinformed or stupid. I have seen a lot of talk around the EU's AI Act that is coming into effect in Aug 2026. So what does it ACTUALLY say (https://t.co/5VQus8K0Bh):

"Transparency risk
This refers to the risks associated with a need for transparency around the use of AI. The AI Act introduces specific disclosure obligations to ensure that humans are informed when necessary to preserve trust. For instance, when using AI systems such as chatbots, humans should be made aware that they are interacting with a machine so they can take an informed decision.

Moreover, providers of generative AI have to ensure that AI-generated content is identifiable. On top of that, certain AI-generated content should be clearly and visibly labelled, namely deep fakes and text published with the purpose to inform the public on matters of public interest.

The transparency rules of the AI Act will come into effect in August 2026."

Lets read some more shall we? (https://t.co/z1zdUy5F9C)
"Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated. Providers shall ensure their technical solutions are effective, interoperable, robust and reliable as far as this is technically feasible, taking into account the specificities and limitations of various types of content, the costs of implementation and the generally acknowledged state of the art, as may be reflected in relevant technical standards. This obligation shall not apply to the extent the AI systems perform an assistive function for standard editing or do not substantially alter the input data provided by the deployer or the semantics thereof, or where authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences."

This WHOLE move and the WHOLE law is to let people know that what they are looking at is AI generated and to make sure that AI companies and any generated AI stuff are watermarked as such. 

As more and more AI generated stuff gets produced, there NEEDS to be a way to tell what is AI and what is real. You, the YTA person might not like it, but regulators and society at large agrees that we should mark what is AI and what is not....

NOW, I think most people probably don't give 2 shits if what they are looking at is AI or not if it is entertaining or provides value. I love watching creative AI videos and shorts that people make. If its good, its good! 

But when you try to pass off AI stuff as real and do it in a sneaky way, it will get flagged as AI. Politics niche is huge and makes a lot of money for a lot of people. Well what happens when there is a shit ton of AI clones and fake AI politics channels (even more than there might already be) with (AI) Trump giving completely fake speeches or talks about things that didn't happen. Or Anti Trump channels saying things like "2 minutes ago! Trump sent to jail" with AI video and audio of things that didn't happen.

Youtube has already said they are not banning AI Voice overs from the platform. We ALL KNOW that inauthentic mainly hits low quality AI mass produced slop. It does hit high quality and real channels as well, but lets not pretend your fuckin 5 image, 2 hour long AI Story was not AI slop for old people...

Around 90% of adults couldn't tell AI videos from real videos according from a study from Runway AI (Take it with a grain of salt). https://t.co/H88ftkP7lV

We were all pretty blown away by Seedance 2's quality. In literally 3 years, the "Will Smith Eating Spaghetti" (2023 - 2026) went from comically bad, to damn realistic.

So in summary:
 Does YouTube have some alternative motive? Probably not. 

Does it give YouTube an easier way to detect AI VO's.
Yes it does.

Will YouTube ban your channel or give it inauthentic content only because you used 11Labs voice?
No it won't.

Should you stop posting super low effort/quality AI Slop if you don't want to run risky channels now?
Yes you should.

Will you probably see an AI tag or disclaimer somewhere when people watch a video with 11Labs or other AI content, even if you don't check the box? Yes they probably will.

Will Youtube fuck your channel over because you used 11Labs before the deadline in August? No, they won't, unless you run obvious AI slop, then its always at risk.

Google and Large Tech don't just jump around with glee and bend over backwards to comply with regulators and governments. They do the bare minimum and mostly maliciously comply. **WHAT HAPPENED**

This week, the two biggest AI companies on earth made moves that have nothing to do with building smarter models — and everything to do with owning the pipe between intelligence and
content:
**WHAT HAPPENED**

This week, the two biggest AI companies on earth made moves that have nothing to do with building smarter models — and everything to do with owning the pipe between intelligence and the enterprise.

On Monday, OpenAI launched the OpenAI Deployment Company, a majority-owned subsidiary backed by more than $4 billion from 19 investment firms including TPG, SoftBank, Goldman Sachs, Bain Capital, and McKinsey. The launch included an agreement to acquire Tomoro, an Edinburgh-based AI consulting firm that has spent two and a half years embedding OpenAI engineers inside companies like Tesco, Virgin Atlantic, Supercell, and the NBA. Tomoro's 150 Forward Deployed Engineers become the founding cadre of what OpenAI is calling "DeployCo."

On Tuesday, at Google I/O, Sundar Pichai unveiled Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini Spark (a 24/7 personal AI agent), and a new $100/month AI Ultra subscription tier — while cutting the top-tier Ultra plan from $250 to $200. Google also announced Gemini Omni (a world model for video), the Antigravity agent-first development platform, and partnerships with Shopify, Salesforce, Macquarie Bank, Ramp, Xero, and Databricks to deploy agentic workflows inside their operations.

Two days. Two companies. One unmistakable signal: the battle has moved from the model to the deployment surface.

**WHAT EVERYONE SAYS**

The headlines are treating these as separate stories. Coverage of OpenAI's Deployment Company frames it as "OpenAI becomes a consulting firm" or "OpenAI copies Palantir." Coverage of Google I/O frames it as "Google catches up in the model race" or "Google launches its ChatGPT competitor."

The conventional take reduces both moves to competitive jockeying — OpenAI wants more enterprise revenue, Google wants to match ChatGPT. Analysts are comparing benchmark scores and subscription prices, debating whether Gemini 3.5 Flash is "as good as" GPT-4.x, and whether $100/month is the right price point for AI Ultra.

This misses the entire point.

**WHAT'S ACTUALLY GOING ON**

The AI industry has crossed an inflection point that most of the coverage hasn't noticed yet: model quality is no longer the binding constraint on enterprise AI adoption. Integration is.

OpenAI has over a million business customers. Its annualized revenue hit $25 billion in February. Enterprise accounts are on pace to match consumer revenue by year-end. And yet OpenAI's own leadership is saying the quiet part out loud: "the gap between using a product and deploying it inside core business operations remains enormous." That's not a model problem. That's a plumbing problem.

This is why OpenAI is spending $4+ billion not on compute or training runs, but on people — Forward Deployed Engineers who sit inside client organizations and build production systems. This is why Google announced partnerships with six major enterprises at I/O specifically around agentic workflow deployment, not just model access. This is why Anthropic built a $1.5 billion joint venture with Blackstone and Goldman Sachs for its own deployment arm. This is why Google committed $750 million to fund partners deploying agentic AI.

The three largest foundation model companies have independently converged on the same conclusion in the same quarter: the money is not in selling intelligence. It is in installing it.

Here's what makes this structural, not tactical:

1. **Switching costs are being built at the deployment layer, not the model layer.** A company that has OpenAI FDEs embedded in its workflows, with custom integrations connecting GPT models to proprietary data pipelines, evaluation harnesses, and governance controls, does not switch to Claude because Anthropic releases a better benchmark score. The relationship generates switching costs that no competing model can erode. Palantir proved this — its FDE model drove commercial revenue up 133% YoY and generated 640% returns for early investors. OpenAI is applying the same logic to a market 100x larger.

2. **The subscription pricing war is a deployment strategy, not a product strategy.** Google's new $100/month AI Ultra tier isn't priced to maximize subscription revenue. It's priced to pull developers and technical leads into the Google AI ecosystem at a price point OpenAI can't match without cannibalizing its own revenue. The 20TB of storage, YouTube Premium, and Antigravity access aren't perks — they're ecosystem lock-in. You don't leave a platform that houses your datasets, your media, your development environment, and your AI agent. The $250-to-$200 price cut on the top tier is a competitive squeeze play: it forces OpenAI to either match on price or concede the power-user segment.

3. **Consulting firms are now infrastructure.** McKinsey, Bain, and Capgemini aren't just advisors to the OpenAI Deployment Company — they're distribution. Their combined client networks represent thousands of enterprises that will now be routed to OpenAI's deployment stack as the default path. This is the AI equivalent of what Microsoft did in the 1990s when it made Windows the default OS for every PC manufacturer. The consulting firms become the channel, and OpenAI's models become the standard.

4. **Google's "free" deployment is the counter-strategy.** While OpenAI charges for embedded engineers, Google is bundling deployment capability into the subscription itself. Gemini Spark, Daily Brief, Antigravity — these are deployment tools wrapped as consumer features. Google's 900 million monthly Gemini users are a deployment surface that no consulting army can match. If Google can make Spark genuinely useful as a 24/7 agent that works across your email, calendar, and documents, it achieves embedded deployment at a scale that no FDE model can reach — because the agent IS the FDE.

**WHAT IT MEANS FOR BUSINESS LEADERS**

1. **Stop evaluating AI vendors by model benchmarks and start evaluating them by deployment infrastructure.** The model you choose today will likely be the third-best option within six months. The deployment relationship — the integrations, the embedded engineers, the custom workflows — will last for years. When choosing between OpenAI, Google, or Anthropic, ask: who will help me make this work in my actual operations, with my actual data, under my actual governance requirements? The answer to that question matters more than any MMLU score.

2. **Negotiate your deployment terms now, before the lock-in solidifies.** We're in a brief window where AI companies are competing aggressively for enterprise relationships. OpenAI's Guaranteed Capacity offering (1-3 year compute commitments with volume discounts) and Google's aggressive subscription pricing are acquisition strategies, not margin optimizations. Once a vendor's engineers are embedded in your operations and their models are wired into your data infrastructure, your negotiating leverage collapses. Lock in favorable terms — pricing, portability, data ownership, exit clauses — while you still have leverage.

3. **Build an internal AI deployment capability, or accept permanent vendor dependency.** The FDE model works because most companies lack the internal expertise to deploy AI in production. If you rely entirely on OpenAI's or Google's engineers to build and maintain your AI workflows, you are renting your competitive advantage from a vendor who also serves your competitors. The companies that will win the AI deployment era are the ones investing in their own AI engineering teams who can work alongside — not depend on — vendor FDEs.

4. **Google's agent-first strategy is the one to watch for mid-market companies.** If you're a company that can't afford OpenAI's embedded engineering engagements or Palantir-style deployments, Google's strategy of bundling deployment capability into consumer subscriptions could be transformative — if Spark delivers. A 24/7 AI agent that works across your Google Workspace stack at $100/month is a fundamentally different value proposition than hiring a consulting firm for a six-figure deployment project. But "if" is doing a lot of work in that sentence. Spark is in beta, trusted testers only, US-only. Don't bet your 2027 roadmap on it. Test it, but maintain alternatives.

5. **The "AI strategy" conversation in your boardroom is probably wrong.** Most enterprises are still framing their AI strategy as a technology decision — which model, which platform, which API. The moves this week confirm that the real strategy question is organizational: how do you restructure workflows, teams, and decision-making processes around AI that can now act autonomously? The companies that figure out the org design question will outperform the companies that only figure out the vendor selection question. Every time.

The model war is over. Nobody won. The deployment war just started.

#AIDeployment #EnterpriseAI #AgenticAI

The 39-year-old Japanese powerhouse, formerly EVIL in New Japan Pro-Wrestling and an ex-IWGP Heavyweight Champion, signed with WWE in April and debuted Tuesday on NXT airing on The CW. The one-of-a-kind card from Topps' 2025 Royalty WWE set features a patch from Orton's WrestleMania 41 match in Las Vegas, signed with 'WM#20' and 'The Viper.' It shattered records by doubling the prior No. 2 WWE card sale, beating out a Steve Austin 1/1, after Knicks star Karl-Anthony Towns bid nearly $40,000 before losing in the final seconds. Orton reacted by promising the winner his WM41 throwback gear—he still has his iconic 2004 SummerSlam trunks from becoming WWE's youngest world champion at age 24. News Lead Up

24 + Hours Ago

BTC/Cryptos

Bitcoin hits the pause button at $80K

Market Overview

The crypto market capitalisation has stalled at around $2.70 trillion, reflecting Bitcoin’s indecision around $80,000. At the same time, risk aversion is mounting in global markets, which can be easily linked to profit-taking following the rally and the US dollar's upward momentum. Among the top coins, the leaders over the past day were Theta (+8.5%), Toncoin (+4.9%) and NEAR Protocol (+2.1%). The underperformers were Dash (-4.2%), Official Trump (-3.5%) and Zcash (-3.5%).

The sentiment index has settled just below the midpoint of the range, recording readings of 47, 48 and 49 over the last three days. At the same time, we continue to note how difficult it is for the crypto market to consolidate at the upper end of the spectrum, which indicates a predominance of bears.

Bitcoin points to much the same thing, having lost its upward momentum as it approached the 200-day moving average. Although this line is trending downwards, the market has failed to break through it for the past six days. On the other hand, as the decline is quite modest, it resembles nothing more than a breather following a rally, leaving a strong chance of growth resuming.

News Background

According to CoinShares, global investments in crypto funds rose by $858 million last week. Investments in Bitcoin increased by $706 million, in Ethereum by $77 million, in Solana by $48 million, and in XRP by $40 million. Outflows from Bitcoin short positions totalling $14 million marked the largest of the year.

Investments rose amid a compromise on stablecoin yields under the CLARITY Act. The Senate Banking Committee is expected to consider the bill next week, CoinShares notes.

Strategy acquired 535 BTC for $43 million last week — at an average price of $80,340 per coin. The week before, the company skipped its weekly BTC purchase ahead of its quarterly report. Strategy now holds 818,869 BTC, purchased for $61.86 billion at an average price of $75,540 per Bitcoin.

Strategy will continue to build up its reserves of the leading cryptocurrency. At the same time, the volume of purchases will significantly exceed any potential sales, stated the company’s founder, Michael Saylor. According to him, it is important to remain a ‘net buyer’ and end each year with more coins than at the start.

Jordi Visser, founder of 22V Research, has increased his investment in Ethereum. In his view, this year will see the start of mass asset tokenisation, which will form the basis for payments by AI agents. For autonomous transactions, they will need digital assets such as Ethereum or stablecoins. (FxPro). (Media Man Peg-On): Can we call Michael Saylor the "King Of Bulls". Awesome PR machine and LinkedIn buzz. Join the dots!

Media Man with Cafe News Media Watercooler

Beer killer? Rise of the vodka RTD

Gold Coast-based drinks maker Hard Fizz emerged at around the time of the pandemic, while the ready-to-drink canned beverage market boomed after the pandemic. Hard Fizz originally focused on alcoholic seltzer drinks, but it is now switching to vodka-based canned drinks, with CEO Wade Tiller saying the change is because you are more limited with flavour when you use seltzer. Hard Fizz's seltzer sales have slumped over the past year, at a time when there is a broader consumer shift to RTDs, while vodka-based light RTDs account for 75 per cent of Australian RTD sales. (RMS)

News

oOh!media rejects $770m offer, triggers bidding war

The board of listed outdoor advertising group oOh!media has advised that it is open to further takeover approaches after spurning two suitors. The company has indicated that it assessed both offers and deemed that neither reflected its intrinsic value. US-based private equity firm I Squared Capital had offered $1.45 per share, valuing its bid at $770m; it had trumped a previous offer from Pacific Equity Partners of $1.40 per share. Brian Han from Morningstar says the rejection of both offers means that oOh!media's directors have effectively put up a 'for auction' sign. (RMS)

News Media

Truescope's co-founder and CEO John Croll contends that Australian companies are not getting much value from traditional media monitoring firms. He says they s are paying large sums of money each year for monthly media intelligence reports that are based on daily press clippings, and are therefore usually out of date before the client receives them; he adds that the analysis in these reports is often outsourced to low-cost workers offshore. In contast, Truescope processes content within minutes of publication and performs sentiment analysis at sentence level rather than story level; it also uses artificial intelligence to produce an executive summary. Croll was previously the CEO of iSentia.

News

AI News

The hidden expenses in banking's AI rollout

Tokens have been described as the hidden cost of using artificial intelligence, with tokens being a basic unit that measures how much data is being processed through autonomous AI models such as Anthropic's Claude. Westpac's CEO Anthony Miller told a recent investment banking conference that the bank was still in the process of working out how to disclose token use and productivity, with the cost of tokens depending on the model used. Noel Williams from PwC says the cost of tokens is definitely something that the big banks need to take into consideration, while Goldman Sachs analysts claimed recently that token consumption would increase 22-fold by 2030 and 55-fold by 2040. (RMS)

Cryptos

Altcoins are surging amid a steady rise in BTC price

Market Overview

The crypto market capitalisation has risen by 0.75% over the past 24 hours, reaching $2.69 trillion. The top three performers are Zcash (+29%), Toncoin (+23%) and Filecoin (+16%). The underperformers are Ethereum (−0.4%), Algorand (−0.5%) and Basic Attention Token (−4.6%).

Bitcoin is approaching $81.5K, continuing its movement within an upward channel and hitting new highs since February. This positive momentum can easily be linked to the continued rise in stock indices, which is boosting risk appetite and bringing a more significant technical battle into view. The leading cryptocurrency is approaching its 200-day moving average (currently at $83.3K); a firm consolidation above this level would be a further sign of bullish dominance. We saw the first such sign – consolidation above the 50-day moving average – exactly one month ago. It is quite likely that, as Bitcoin approaches $83K, a short-term profit-taking phase awaits, allowing some of the gains to be taken.

The performance of altcoins clearly shows how BTC’s steady growth is encouraging increased risk-taking. First Toncoin, and today Zcash, have gained nearly 30% over the past 24 hours. The latter has been rising every day since 3 April, gaining 80% during this period; it was one of the first major cryptocurrencies to climb out of the slump at the end of January and reach highs last seen in November of last year. The key pivot zone in 2018 and 2025, near $800, looks well within reach in the coming days.

News Background

The total USDT market capitalisation has increased by $5.9 billion over the last 60 days, whereas prior to March, the market was losing around $2 billion monthly, notes analyst Darkfost. The inflow of capital into the crypto market is boosting asset values.

Morgan Stanley suggests that US banks may be able to hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets in the future, despite current regulatory barriers. The bank recently launched a Bitcoin-based exchange-traded product (ETP). Later this year, Morgan Stanley will launch spot trading in cryptocurrency on its Wealth platform.

The international payment system Western Union has launched its own stablecoin, USDPT, on the Solana blockchain. Integration with SOL will allow the company to speed up settlements and move away from traditional interbank systems, which are prone to delays.

BitMine has increased its Ethereum reserves to $13 billion, purchasing over 100,000 ETH for the third week in a row. The company’s reserves have reached 5,180,131 ETH, or 4.29% of the Ethereum supply.

Toncoin (TON) jumped by 45% amid fee reductions and the reorganisation of TON. Pavel Durov announced that Telegram would take over management of the TON crypto project from the current operator, the TON Foundation. The entrepreneur promised to reduce fees on the TON network sixfold and turn the eponymous token into a mass-market product.

News

Advertising expectations and experience: Australians have their say about AI

The second wave of Ad Standards' Community Sentiment Tracker, which was conducted by Roy Morgan, has found that 72% of Australians are concerned about the use of AI-generated content in advertising, particularly its potential to mislead or deceive people with unrealistic or fake content. Around half are also worried that the use of AI could reduce authenticity and creativity in advertising and promote unrealistic body or beauty standards. Australians believe AI-generated content is already widely used in advertising, with more than half saying that it is used very often (21%) or often (37%). Despite this, confidence in recognising AI-generated content remains low, with one in five Australians saying they are not at all confident they could identify when AI-generated content has been used in an ad. Some 64% of Australians believe it should always be necessary to disclose when advertising contains AI-generated content. The Ad Standards-Roy Morgan Community Sentiment Tracker Survey was conducted online with a cross-section of 1,000 Australians aged 18+ between 19 February and 2 March 2026. (Roy Morgan)

Southern Cross Media Group's CEO Rohan Lund has indicated that the Seven Network owner could potentially bid for the NRL's broadcasting rights. Lund says media companies like Seven have an important role in helping audiences and partners to connect with their sports teams. He adds that Seven could be interested in the annual State of Origin series in particular. The Nine Network's current free-to-air rights deal for the NRL expires next year, and the NRL aims to finalise its next deal by the end of July. (RMS)

Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta Platforms Report Q1 2026 Earnings Beating Expectations

Alphabet reported Q1 2026 revenue of $109.9 billion and EPS of $5.11, surpassing estimates, with Google Cloud revenue up 63% to $20 billion.

Bitcoin has begun hunting down short sellers

Market Overview

The crypto market capitalisation has continued to hit new highs since early February, reaching $2.67 trillion. This time, the movement was not uniform, consisting of individual surges led by Toncoin (+29%), followed by Algorand (+4.5%) and Basic Attention Token (+4%). The underperformers include Dash (-5.5%), Aptos (-2.1%) and VeChain (-1.6%).

The sentiment index has reached 50, the midpoint of the indicator’s range, where it last stood on 17 January. The market is approaching a significant turning point. Since last October, there have been only brief surges in sentiment to higher levels, but these have provided excellent opportunities for bears to sell at higher prices.

Although Bitcoin faced some pressure midday on Monday, it overcame it on Tuesday, reaching $81K and gaining 1.3% for the day, though, by and large, it covered this ground in just the last 4 hours. We attribute this rally to short squeezes, as the rise occurred during the period of the most aggressive movements ahead of the start of active trading in Asia, when liquidity is at its lowest. Meanwhile, on the stock markets, there was only a slight pullback following the downward momentum. In any case, on the daily charts, Bitcoin is recording its sixth bullish candle, and the entire April uptrend now fits within a new upward channel, with the upper boundary currently at the 200-day moving average.

News Background

The Capriole investment fund has noted a sharp rise in demand for Bitcoin from major players. Institutional investors are buying up more than 500% of the daily mining output of the leading cryptocurrency every day. Historically, such a supply shortage has led to a 24% rise in BTC over the following month.

Bitcoin appears poised for an upward surge. A break above $80K opens up the possibility of reaching $86K–$88K in the coming period, notes MN Trading founder Michael van de Poppe.

Hard Fizz's seltzer sales have slumped over the past year, at a time when there is a broader consumer shift to RTDs, while vodka-based light RTDs account for 75 per cent of Australian RTD sales. US-based private equity firm I Squared Capital had offered $1.45 per share, valuing its bid at $770m; it had trumped a previous offer from Pacific Equity Partners of $1.40 per share. In contast, Truescope processes content within minutes of publication and performs sentiment analysis at sentence level rather than story level; it also uses artificial intelligence to produce an executive summary. Advertising expectations and experience: Australians have their say about AI

The second wave of Ad Standards' Community Sentiment Tracker, which was conducted by Roy Morgan, has found that 72% of Australians are concerned about the use of AI-generated content in advertising, particularly its potential to mislead or deceive people with unrealistic or fake content. Around half are also worried that the use of AI could reduce authenticity and creativity in advertising and promote unrealistic body or beauty standards. Australians believe AI-generated content is already widely used in advertising, with more than half saying that it is used very often (21%) or often (37%). Hard Fizz originally focused on alcoholic seltzer drinks, but it is now switching to vodka-based canned drinks, with CEO Wade Tiller saying the change is because you are more limited with flavour when you use seltzer. Hard Fizz's seltzer sales have slumped over the past year, at a time when there is a broader consumer shift to RTDs, while vodka-based light RTDs account for 75 per cent of Australian RTD sales. (RMS)

US-based private equity firm I Squared Capital had offered $1.45 per share, valuing its bid at $770m; it had trumped a previous offer from Pacific Equity Partners of $1.40 per share. ASX ends lower after CSL's $9b wipeout

The Australian sharemarket lost ground on Monday, amid fading hopes of a permanent ceasefire in the Middle East; the S&P/ASX 200 shed 0.5 per cent to close at 8,701.8 points. CSL was down 16 per cent at $100.75 and the ANZ Bank fell 2.5 per cent to end the session at $35.88. News

Beer killer? Rise of the vodka RTD

Gold Coast-based drinks maker Hard Fizz emerged at around the time of the pandemic, while the ready-to-drink canned beverage market boomed after the pandemic. Hard Fizz originally focused on alcoholic seltzer drinks, but it is now switching to vodka-based canned drinks, with CEO Wade Tiller saying the change is because you are more limited with flavour when you use seltzer. Hard Fizz's seltzer sales have slumped over the past year, at a time when there is a broader consumer shift to RTDs, while vodka-based light RTDs account for 75 per cent of Australian RTD sales. (RMS)

oOh!media rejects $770m offer, triggers bidding war

The board of listed outdoor advertising group oOh!media has advised that it is open to further takeover approaches after spurning two suitors. The company has indicated that it assessed both offers and deemed that neither reflected its intrinsic value. US-based private equity firm I Squared Capital had offered $1.45 per share, valuing its bid at $770m; it had trumped a previous offer from Pacific Equity Partners of $1.40 per share. Brian Han from Morningstar says the rejection of both offers means that oOh!media's directors have effectively put up a 'for auction' sign. (RMS)

News Mwsi

Truescope's co-founder and CEO John Croll contends that Australian companies are not getting much value from traditional media monitoring firms. He says they s are paying large sums of money each year for monthly media intelligence reports that are based on daily press clippings, and are therefore usually out of date before the client receives them; he adds that the analysis in these reports is often outsourced to low-cost workers offshore. In contast, Truescope processes content within minutes of publication and performs sentiment analysis at sentence level rather than story level; it also uses artificial intelligence to produce an executive summary. Croll was previously the CEO of iSentia.

The hidden expenses in banking's AI rollout

Tokens have been described as the hidden cost of using artificial intelligence, with tokens being a basic unit that measures how much data is being processed through autonomous AI models such as Anthropic's Claude. Westpac's CEO Anthony Miller told a recent investment banking conference that the bank was still in the process of working out how to disclose token use and productivity, with the cost of tokens depending on the model used. Noel Williams from PwC says the cost of tokens is definitely something that the big banks need to take into consideration, while Goldman Sachs analysts claimed recently that token consumption would increase 22-fold by 2030 and 55-fold by 2040. Roberts contends its rejection by the ASX was sign of Australia's unwillingness to " back next-generation technology at scale", while Iren has signed a $4.7bn deal with Nvidia to house its processing chips in Iren data centres.

China hit with punitive 82pc steel tariff

The federal government has imposed tariffs of between 38 per cent and 82 per cent on hot-rolled coil steel products that are imported from China. Industry Minister Tim Ayres approved the new tariffs on Monday, with temporary levies of up 117 per cent having been in place since late 2025 while the Anti-Dumping Commission completed its investigation into claims that China was exporting steel products to Australia at heavily discounted prices. A spokesman for Ayres says that all trade remedies are fully consistent with Australia's obligations under its trade agreements, and the nation's anti-dumping regime does not target any country in particular.

Advertising expectations and experience: Australians have their say about AI

The second wave of Ad Standards' Community Sentiment Tracker, which was conducted by Roy Morgan, has found that 72% of Australians are concerned about the use of AI-generated content in advertising, particularly its potential to mislead or deceive people with unrealistic or fake content. Around half are also worried that the use of AI could reduce authenticity and creativity in advertising and promote unrealistic body or beauty standards. Australians believe AI-generated content is already widely used in advertising, with more than half saying that it is used very often (21%) or often (37%). Despite this, confidence in recognising AI-generated content remains low, with one in five Australians saying they are not at all confident they could identify when AI-generated content has been used in an ad. Some 64% of Australians believe it should always be necessary to disclose when advertising contains AI-generated content. The Ad Standards-Roy Morgan Community Sentiment Tracker Survey was conducted online with a cross-section of 1,000 Australians aged 18+ between 19 February and 2 March 2026. (Roy Morgan)

Geopolitics has caused the dollar to retreat

The end of Operation Epic Fury is boosting risk appetite.

Japan is likely to continue punishing speculators. The US dollar has lost ground following statements from the White House regarding the conclusion of the two-month ‘Operation Epic Fury’ and progress in negotiations with Iran. Investors are interpreting this as a de-escalation in the Middle East and are selling Brent. At the same time, the dollar index is once again testing the lows of the past two months amid risk-on sentiment in key markets. Optimism could push EURUSD higher. Although its further trajectory will depend on the pace of the fall in oil prices. It will take time to repair the damaged energy infrastructure in the Persian Gulf. Therefore, it is believed that Brent and WTI will not return to the $65–70 levels seen before the conflict in the Middle East this year. This is a pro-inflationary factor. US services PMI indices are signalling the highest price pressure since 2022, while the futures market is ramping up expectations of Fed rate hikes. It will not be easy for Kevin Warsh to fulfil Donald Trump’s wishes for a significant easing of policy. For now, traders’ attention is entirely focused on the Middle East. The end of the conflict is driving the EURUSD up to 1.1760, and this rise will gain momentum with further signs of de-escalation.

Conversely, another breakdown in negotiations and a deadlock in US-Iran relations will force the major currency pair to take a step back. And this is not merely a matter of caution, as alongside their conciliatory rhetoric, the US is building up its military presence in the Persian Gulf. The sharp collapse in USDJPY on Wednesday suggests that the government has once again intervened in the forex market. Japan needs to properly deter speculators from using dips in the US dollar to buy it. Rumours of a de-escalation in geopolitical tensions have catalysed a rally of more than 3% in gold, pushing it above $4,700. The fall in oil prices reduces the risk of high inflation becoming entrenched and removes the need for central banks to tighten policy. May 12

ASX ends lower after CSL's $9b wipeout

The Australian sharemarket lost ground on Monday, amid fading hopes of a permanent ceasefire in the Middle East; the S&P/ASX 200 shed 0.5 per cent to close at 8,701.8 points. CSL was down 16 per cent at $100.75 and the ANZ Bank fell 2.5 per cent to end the session at $35.88. However, Woodside Energy rose 1.5 per cent to $30.51, Inghams was up 7.4 per cent at $1.82 and Dyno Nobel finished 6.6 per cent higher at $3.54. (RMS)

News

Beer killer? Rise of the vodka RTD

Gold Coast-based drinks maker Hard Fizz emerged at around the time of the pandemic, while the ready-to-drink canned beverage market boomed after the pandemic. Hard Fizz originally focused on alcoholic seltzer drinks, but it is now switching to vodka-based canned drinks, with CEO Wade Tiller saying the change is because you are more limited with flavour when you use seltzer. Hard Fizz's seltzer sales have slumped over the past year, at a time when there is a broader consumer shift to RTDs, while vodka-based light RTDs account for 75 per cent of Australian RTD sales. (RMS)

News

oOh!media rejects $770m offer, triggers bidding war

The board of listed outdoor advertising group oOh!media has advised that it is open to further takeover approaches after spurning two suitors. The company has indicated that it assessed both offers and deemed that neither reflected its intrinsic value. US-based private equity firm I Squared Capital had offered $1.45 per share, valuing its bid at $770m; it had trumped a previous offer from Pacific Equity Partners of $1.40 per share. Brian Han from Morningstar says the rejection of both offers means that oOh!media's directors have effectively put up a 'for auction' sign. (RMS)

News Mwsi

Truescope's co-founder and CEO John Croll contends that Australian companies are not getting much value from traditional media monitoring firms. He says they s are paying large sums of money each year for monthly media intelligence reports that are based on daily press clippings, and are therefore usually out of date before the client receives them; he adds that the analysis in these reports is often outsourced to low-cost workers offshore. In contast, Truescope processes content within minutes of publication and performs sentiment analysis at sentence level rather than story level; it also uses artificial intelligence to produce an executive summary. Croll was previously the CEO of iSentia.

News

AI News

The hidden expenses in banking's AI rollout

Tokens have been described as the hidden cost of using artificial intelligence, with tokens being a basic unit that measures how much data is being processed through autonomous AI models such as Anthropic's Claude. Westpac's CEO Anthony Miller told a recent investment banking conference that the bank was still in the process of working out how to disclose token use and productivity, with the cost of tokens depending on the model used. Noel Williams from PwC says the cost of tokens is definitely something that the big banks need to take into consideration, while Goldman Sachs analysts claimed recently that token consumption would increase 22-fold by 2030 and 55-fold by 2040. (RMS)

News

AI/Aviation (Aust)

Union demands Qantas AI talks

The Australian Services Union has asked for a meeting with Qantas CEO Vanessa Hudson, following comments by her at a recent conference that suggest she intends to accelerate the airline's adoption of artificial intelligence. With the ASU representing clerical and call centre staff at Qantas, assistant national secretary Scott Cohen said attempts to enshrine protections into work agreements for staff around the implementation of AI had not been agreed to by Qantas, making Hudson's comments all the more concerning; he says he hopes that the ASU can work with Qantas to find ways by which AI can improve customer service and perhaps even lead to more human interaction. (RMS)

AI News

'Red tape is killing Australia's AI dream'

Data centre company Iren was called Iris Energy and operated as a bitcoin miner when it tried to list on the ASX in 2021, but the ASX knocked it back. That proved a blessing in disguise, as Iren instead floated on the tech-heavy Nasdaq exchange in the US, with co-founder Dan Roberts noting that on Friday it traded $US10bn in just that one session, which he says is more than the ASX's on-market dail turnover of $7.5bn. Roberts contends its rejection by the ASX was sign of Australia's unwillingness to " back next-generation technology at scale", while Iren has signed a $4.7bn deal with Nvidia to house its processing chips in Iren data centres.

News

Australia

China hit with punitive 82pc steel tariff

The federal government has imposed tariffs of between 38 per cent and 82 per cent on hot-rolled coil steel products that are imported from China. Industry Minister Tim Ayres approved the new tariffs on Monday, with temporary levies of up 117 per cent having been in place since late 2025 while the Anti-Dumping Commission completed its investigation into claims that China was exporting steel products to Australia at heavily discounted prices. A spokesman for Ayres says that all trade remedies are fully consistent with Australia's obligations under its trade agreements, and the nation's anti-dumping regime does not target any country in particular.

Trump Hosts UFC Stars in Oval Office for White House Fight Event

Trump welcomed lightweight champ Ilia Topuria, challenger Justin Gaethje, light heavyweight titleholder Alex Pereira, and heavyweight Ciryl Gane to preview UFC Freedom 250 on June 14. The free event on the South Lawn features a 4,500-seat arena for Topuria vs. Gaethje and Pereira vs. Gane, tying into America's 250th anniversary and Trump's 80th birthday, with overflow crowds on giant screens nearby. Banter flew in the meeting—Trump joked about Pereira's powerful hand, while Topuria teased him lightly—building hype for this historic first pro sports event on White House grounds. News Lead Up

60 + Hours Ago

Cryptos

Altcoins are surging amid a steady rise in BTC price

Market Overview

The crypto market capitalisation has risen by 0.75% over the past 24 hours, reaching $2.69 trillion. The top three performers are Zcash (+29%), Toncoin (+23%) and Filecoin (+16%). The underperformers are Ethereum (−0.4%), Algorand (−0.5%) and Basic Attention Token (−4.6%).

Bitcoin is approaching $81.5K, continuing its movement within an upward channel and hitting new highs since February. This positive momentum can easily be linked to the continued rise in stock indices, which is boosting risk appetite and bringing a more significant technical battle into view. The leading cryptocurrency is approaching its 200-day moving average (currently at $83.3K); a firm consolidation above this level would be a further sign of bullish dominance. We saw the first such sign – consolidation above the 50-day moving average – exactly one month ago. It is quite likely that, as Bitcoin approaches $83K, a short-term profit-taking phase awaits, allowing some of the gains to be taken.

The performance of altcoins clearly shows how BTC’s steady growth is encouraging increased risk-taking. First Toncoin, and today Zcash, have gained nearly 30% over the past 24 hours. The latter has been rising every day since 3 April, gaining 80% during this period; it was one of the first major cryptocurrencies to climb out of the slump at the end of January and reach highs last seen in November of last year. The key pivot zone in 2018 and 2025, near $800, looks well within reach in the coming days.

News Background

The total USDT market capitalisation has increased by $5.9 billion over the last 60 days, whereas prior to March, the market was losing around $2 billion monthly, notes analyst Darkfost. The inflow of capital into the crypto market is boosting asset values.

Morgan Stanley suggests that US banks may be able to hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets in the future, despite current regulatory barriers. The bank recently launched a Bitcoin-based exchange-traded product (ETP). Later this year, Morgan Stanley will launch spot trading in cryptocurrency on its Wealth platform.

The international payment system Western Union has launched its own stablecoin, USDPT, on the Solana blockchain. Integration with SOL will allow the company to speed up settlements and move away from traditional interbank systems, which are prone to delays.

BitMine has increased its Ethereum reserves to $13 billion, purchasing over 100,000 ETH for the third week in a row. The company’s reserves have reached 5,180,131 ETH, or 4.29% of the Ethereum supply.

Toncoin (TON) jumped by 45% amid fee reductions and the reorganisation of TON. Pavel Durov announced that Telegram would take over management of the TON crypto project from the current operator, the TON Foundation. The entrepreneur promised to reduce fees on the TON network sixfold and turn the eponymous token into a mass-market product.

News

Advertising expectations and experience: Australians have their say about AI

The second wave of Ad Standards' Community Sentiment Tracker, which was conducted by Roy Morgan, has found that 72% of Australians are concerned about the use of AI-generated content in advertising, particularly its potential to mislead or deceive people with unrealistic or fake content. Around half are also worried that the use of AI could reduce authenticity and creativity in advertising and promote unrealistic body or beauty standards. Australians believe AI-generated content is already widely used in advertising, with more than half saying that it is used very often (21%) or often (37%). Despite this, confidence in recognising AI-generated content remains low, with one in five Australians saying they are not at all confident they could identify when AI-generated content has been used in an ad. Some 64% of Australians believe it should always be necessary to disclose when advertising contains AI-generated content. The Ad Standards-Roy Morgan Community Sentiment Tracker Survey was conducted online with a cross-section of 1,000 Australians aged 18+ between 19 February and 2 March 2026. (Roy Morgan)

Southern Cross Media Group's CEO Rohan Lund has indicated that the Seven Network owner could potentially bid for the NRL's broadcasting rights. Lund says media companies like Seven have an important role in helping audiences and partners to connect with their sports teams. He adds that Seven could be interested in the annual State of Origin series in particular. The Nine Network's current free-to-air rights deal for the NRL expires next year, and the NRL aims to finalise its next deal by the end of July. (RMS)

60 Hours Ago

Geopolitics has caused the dollar to retreat

The end of Operation Epic Fury is boosting risk appetite.

Japan is likely to continue punishing speculators. The US dollar has lost ground following statements from the White House regarding the conclusion of the two-month ‘Operation Epic Fury’ and progress in negotiations with Iran. Investors are interpreting this as a de-escalation in the Middle East and are selling Brent. At the same time, the dollar index is once again testing the lows of the past two months amid risk-on sentiment in key markets. Optimism could push EURUSD higher. Although its further trajectory will depend on the pace of the fall in oil prices. It will take time to repair the damaged energy infrastructure in the Persian Gulf. Therefore, it is believed that Brent and WTI will not return to the $65–70 levels seen before the conflict in the Middle East this year. This is a pro-inflationary factor. US services PMI indices are signalling the highest price pressure since 2022, while the futures market is ramping up expectations of Fed rate hikes. It will not be easy for Kevin Warsh to fulfil Donald Trump’s wishes for a significant easing of policy. For now, traders’ attention is entirely focused on the Middle East. The end of the conflict is driving the EURUSD up to 1.1760, and this rise will gain momentum with further signs of de-escalation.

Conversely, another breakdown in negotiations and a deadlock in US-Iran relations will force the major currency pair to take a step back. And this is not merely a matter of caution, as alongside their conciliatory rhetoric, the US is building up its military presence in the Persian Gulf. The sharp collapse in USDJPY on Wednesday suggests that the government has once again intervened in the forex market. Japan needs to properly deter speculators from using dips in the US dollar to buy it. Rumours of a de-escalation in geopolitical tensions have catalysed a rally of more than 3% in gold, pushing it above $4,700. The fall in oil prices reduces the risk of high inflation becoming entrenched and removes the need for central banks to tighten policy. As a result, the precious metal may see a return to the debasement trade. (FxPro)

News Lead Up

72 Hours Ago

Bitcoin has begun hunting down short sellers

Market Overview

The crypto market capitalisation has continued to hit new highs since early February, reaching $2.67 trillion. This time, the movement was not uniform, consisting of individual surges led by Toncoin (+29%), followed by Algorand (+4.5%) and Basic Attention Token (+4%). The underperformers include Dash (-5.5%), Aptos (-2.1%) and VeChain (-1.6%).

The sentiment index has reached 50, the midpoint of the indicator’s range, where it last stood on 17 January. The market is approaching a significant turning point. Since last October, there have been only brief surges in sentiment to higher levels, but these have provided excellent opportunities for bears to sell at higher prices.

Although Bitcoin faced some pressure midday on Monday, it overcame it on Tuesday, reaching $81K and gaining 1.3% for the day, though, by and large, it covered this ground in just the last 4 hours. We attribute this rally to short squeezes, as the rise occurred during the period of the most aggressive movements ahead of the start of active trading in Asia, when liquidity is at its lowest. Meanwhile, on the stock markets, there was only a slight pullback following the downward momentum. In any case, on the daily charts, Bitcoin is recording its sixth bullish candle, and the entire April uptrend now fits within a new upward channel, with the upper boundary currently at the 200-day moving average.

News Background

The Capriole investment fund has noted a sharp rise in demand for Bitcoin from major players. Institutional investors are buying up more than 500% of the daily mining output of the leading cryptocurrency every day. Historically, such a supply shortage has led to a 24% rise in BTC over the following month.

Bitcoin appears poised for an upward surge. A break above $80K opens up the possibility of reaching $86K–$88K in the coming period, notes MN Trading founder Michael van de Poppe.

Following the latest adjustment, Bitcoin’s mining difficulty has fallen by 2.3% to 132.47 T. According to Glassnode, the network’s average hash rate, smoothed by a 7-day moving average, stands at around 955 EH/s.

Senators Tom Tillis and Angela Olsbrooks have reached a compromise regarding stablecoin yields in the CLARITY Act. This bill regulating the US crypto market may be considered by the Senate Banking Committee in the week following 11 May. (FxPro)

BHP's price deal puts minnows, rivals on alert

Rio Tinto's former CEO Sam Walsh believes that the iron ore pricing deal between BHP and China Mineral Resources Group will fail. Few details of the deal to end the long-running dispute between BHP and CMRG have emerged, although reports suggest that BHP has ceded more influence to China in setting iron ore prices; this could potentially lead to more ore being priced in Chinese currency. Geoff Raby, Australian ambassador to China, believes that the key outcome of the deal is BHP's acceptance that the benchmark price of iron ore should be set by China, rather than a price reporting agency based in the US or the UK. (ABIX)

content:
I've worked with over a thousand YT clients.

Exactly ZERO of them have lost their channel. 

Some of them have gotten strikes. 

That happens. 

But none of them have been fully terminated.

And I've watched enough channels go down to know exactly what gets you flagged.

If you're in a health or money niche, study YMYL. That stands for Your Money or Your Life, and it's the same framework Google uses for SEO. YouTube applies similar logic. If your content touches someone's finances or health, you're under a microscope.

FIRST: take the dollar signs out of your thumbnails and titles.

YouTube's AI scans for risk signals. A dollar sign in the title or thumbnail is a red flag that triggers a closer look at your channel. And once the system starts looking, it's going to find something.

It's like getting audited. Don't get audited in the first place.

Instead of "How to Make $100K from Dropshipping," 
Just say "How to Make Six Figures from Dropshipping." 

Same message, way less risk.

SECOND: put a disclaimer at the beginning of your videos.

Verbal and visual. 

Something simple. "This is educational content, not financial or legal advice. If you need help with those things, please consult a professional."

It takes 10 seconds and it futureproofs your brand.

THIRD: check https://t.co/nPCHGh23D0 before you pick a niche.

That site tracks which channels are getting terminated. If you see a pattern of channels getting nuked in a specific niche, stay out of it. You can also use VidIQ and look for channels with negative view counts, that usually means they got striked and started deleting videos.

FOURTH: stay away from full AI-generated content.

YouTube is deleting channels that pretend to be real when they're fully AI slop. If you use AI to make the entire video, thumbnail to script to voiceover, you're going to get flagged.

AI is a tool. Use it to make your videos better. Don't use it to replace yourself entirely.

I had to learn this lesson myself. We stopped making remote job videos because YouTube warned us about the niche. We had over 1,000 verified testimonials of getting people jobs. Didn't matter. YouTube flagged the niche because of all the scam channels in it, and we had to pivot.

If you get two strikes, go into survival mode. There's a process that works about 70-80% of the time to get strikes removed, and there are things you can do to make it nearly impossible to get a third.

Protecting your channel is part of running a YT business. Not an afterthought.

content:
1000人超を指導してきて、AI副業で安定して稼いでいる人に共通するパターンが見えてきた。

技術力でも努力量でもない。「手を動かす前に考える時間」の長さだ。

稼げていない人のパターン:
・ツールを触りながら考える
・「とりあえず作ってみる」から始める
・失敗してから「何がしたかったか」を考える

稼いでいる人のパターン:
・クライアントの問題を整理してから手を動かす
・「作る前の設計」に全体工数の40%を使う
・AIに渡す前に「期待する出力」を書き出す

─────────────────────
具体的な違いを見せる
─────────────────────

同じ「LINE自動応答を作ってほしい」という依頼でも：

A（稼げていない）:
→ LINEのAPIを調べ始める
→ Webhookを試す
→ Claude APIと繋ごうとする
→ 2週間後「なんとなく動く」ものが完成
→ 単価: 5万円

B（稼いでいる）:
→ 「どんなメッセージに何を返してほしいか」を最初に整理
→ フロー図を書く（30分）
→ Claude Codeに型スケルトンと仕様書を渡す
→ 3日後に「完全に仕様通りに動く」ものを納品
→ 単価: 20万円

違いは技術力ではない。「設計に時間をかけたか」だ。

─────────────────────
設計ファーストの実践
─────────────────────

    クライアントから依頼を受ける
           ↓
    「誰が・いつ・何のために使うか」を書く
           ↓
    入力と出力を定義する
           ↓
    例外ケースを3つ考える
           ↓
    初めてClaude Codeを開く

この順番を守るだけで、納品物の品質が変わる。DevAIコミュニティで実証済みだ。

AI時代に稼ぐ力は「思考の質」に移ってきている。あなたは今、思考に時間を使えているか？

content:
改めて配信者が集まるGTA5/FiveMなどのマルチサーバー内で利用する音楽とその著作権について整理してみた。（結構誤解してる人も大勢いるようなので…）
どうしても明確になっていないグレーゾーンは存在していて、過去の経験や自分の匙加減みたいなものも一部含まれてます。
※一応AIでのファクトチェック済み

まず大前提として、ストリーマー向けマルチサーバーの場合、「誰か1人の不注意で、その場にいる不特定多数の配信に半強制的に音楽が流れ、最悪の場合、全員のチャンネルがBANや収益化停止に追い込まれる」という可能性があります。これ、本当に重大で怖いリスクですよね。

原因となる権利関係は、主に下記の4つに整理されます。
1. 著作権（メロディや歌詞の権利）
2. 原盤権（録音された音源そのものの権利）
3. フリー素材の利用規約（サイトごとのルール）
4. AI制作物のサービス規約（生成ツールのルール）

これらを正しく把握しておかないと、知らぬ間に大切な配信者仲間のチャンネルに大迷惑をかけてしまうかもしれません。

1. 著作権（歌詞やメロディ）
音楽の場合、歌詞やメロディが著作物。
こちらはJASRACやNexToneなどの管理団体がYouTubeやTwitchと包括契約を結んでいるため、「自分で歌う・演奏する・DTMで打ち込む」という形であれば、基本的には利用可能。
ただし、YouTubeではContent IDの仕組みによりカバー曲配信の収益の一部が著作者に分配される（収益が減る）リスクがあります。
また、Twitchにはこの自動分配システムがないため、カバーであってもアーカイブが無音化されるなどの影響が出る場合があります。
よって、ゲーム内でアカペラであっても、歌っているそばに他の配信者がいる場合は、周囲の配信者を巻き込んでこの著作権リスクを発生させてしまうことになります。（結構誤解している人が多い）

2. 原盤権（音源そのもの）
多くの人が著作権とごっちゃになっているのがこれ。
これはCDや配信データなど「音源そのもの」の権利で、レコード会社などが管理しています。
原盤権はプラットフォームの包括契約の対象外なので、市販の曲をそのままゲーム内で流す場合、音源単位での権利処理（個別許諾）が必要。
まあ、現実的に不可能です。不特定多数の配信者に各自で処理してもらうなんて到底無理ですよね。
つまり、「市販の音楽をそのまま流す行為」は一発アウトです。
（TwitchのDJプログラムはこれをクリアしている特別なサービス。ただ、あちらはDJ配信専用の仕組みで、ゲーム配信のBGMとして利用することは認められていないんですよね）

3. フリー素材の利用規約
「フリー素材（著作権フリー）」と謳うサイトは多数ありますが、商用利用や利用範囲の規約はバラバラ。
今回のマルチサーバーのようなケースでは、自分が流したBGMが他人の配信に載ると、二次利用・再配布になるリスクがあります。
サイトによっては「動画制作者本人のバックで流すのはいいが、他人のコンテンツへの映り込みはNG」という規約になっている場合もあり、これに抵触すると『著作権侵害』になってしまいます。
「フリー」という言葉を鵜呑みにせず、規約の確認が必須です。

4. AIでの音源制作（SunoやUdioなど）
最近増えているAI生成の音源についてです。
法律や事例がまだまだ整備中の段階ですが、現時点のポイントは以下の通りです。

a. AI生成物の著作権：人間がプロンプト（指示文）を入力して1発で出力しただけの音源には、そもそも著作権（独占権）が無いという見方が強いです。そのため、身内で使う分には「誰かから著作権を主張されてトラブルになるリスク」は低いと言えます。
b. 既存曲との類似性：万が一、AIが作った曲が既存の有名曲に酷似していて著作権侵害（Content IDの誤検知など）となった場合、ペナルティを受けるのはAIの作者ではなく、それを配信で流した「各配信チャンネル」になります。
c. AI生成においての依拠性：著作権侵害は「類似性（似ているか）」に加えて「依拠性（元ネタを参考にしたか）」があるかの両方で判断されます。自分が「意図的に真似しようとしていない」としても、AIが裏でその曲を学習していれば、法的には依拠性があるとみなされるリスクは少なからず存在します。

現時点では、有料プランなどで商用利用権をクリアしたAI音源は、規約のややこしいフリー音源よりはコントロールしやすい側面もあります。
ただ、世の中の流れとして「ゲームやコンテンツにAI生成物を使うこと」自体への反発や炎上リスクもあるため、取り扱いには慎重さが必要だなと感じています。
僕自身も判断が難しいなと感じる事が多くありました…。

まとめとしては、自分で作詞作曲し、自分で演奏・録音した音源でない限りは、必ず原盤権や利用規約の確認が必要だということ。
AI生成については、しっかりと権利関係（有料サービスの利用など）をクリアした上で、ガイドラインを明確にして利用する分には有効な手段になり得ます。
ただ、事前に動画をYouTube等にアップロードしてContent IDに引っかからないかチェックするなど、「知らぬ間に既存の曲に似てしまっていた」という事態を防ぐための確認作業は必須ですし、世界中のどの音楽と似ているのかなんて知りようが無いのでリスクを0にすることは現時点では難しいでしょうね。あと、ガイドラインが無い音源の場合、後からContent ID登録されて、大量のアーカイブに後から影響が出るということも考えられます。

ストリーマーが集まるマルチサーバーって楽しい半面、注意しないといけない点も多いので少しでもこの投稿で理解が進めば良いなと思い投稿してみました。

結局のところ、0から音楽を生み出せるミュージシャンはとっても尊く凄いということ！！

content:
■ 核心
従来のUGC（ユーザー生成風）広告は「撮影コストが高すぎる」問題があった。
https://t.co/P1Kd84cHcZは1,000人以上の超リアルAIアクターを使い、誰でもプロ級の広告動画を爆速で量産可能に。
「企業っぽいAI臭」を徹底排除した自然さが最大の武器です。
■ 主要機能
・300〜1,000+のリアルAIアクター（自作アバターもOK）
・句読点まで反応する自然なText-to-Speech
・頭の傾き・表情変化にも完璧に同期するLip-sync
・「眉の動き・指差し・苛立ち顔」など素人らしいGestureを先にロック（これが一番大事！）
・90秒で放送品質の肌・生地質感が出力（TikTok圧縮にも耐える）
■ 利用方法
1.  https://t.co/P1Kd84cHcZにアクセス（https://t.co/7VvULauBnP）
2.  テキストで商品説明＋トーンを入力
3.  AIアクターを選択 → ノードベースで微調整
4.  1.5分待つだけで完成！ Starterプラン（月110ドル）で月10本、Creatorプラン（月220ドル）で月20本作れます（1本あたり約11ドル）。
■ 背景と実績
ある男性がこのツールで構築したパイプラインだけで、eコマースブランドから1キャンペーン128,000ドルの売上を叩き出した事例あり（変換率1.25%）。
今や5,000社以上が利用中。
マネタイズ案（初心者でもすぐ始められる）
1.  自社D2C商品に即活用 → 広告費激減で利益率爆上げ
2.  UGC動画制作代行 → 1本数万円で請け負い、月数十本で高単価ビジネス
3.  Arcads公式アフィリエイト → 紹介で25% recurring（12ヶ月間）。10人紹介で月573ドル、100人なら5,730ドル可能
4.  AI広告クリエイティブエージェンシー → 小規模ブランド向けにArcads活用パッケージを売る
初心者でも「テキスト打つだけ」でプロ級動画が作れる時代になりました。
これから広告業界が本気で変わります。

•背景：刑法第175条（わいせつ物頒布等罪）違反の摘発事例・有罪判例の増加。モザイク不十分なコンテンツが警察の捜査対象となり、プラットフォーム運営者・クリエイター双方に逮捕リスクが生じている。
•指摘内容：修正基準の甘さがプラットフォーム全体の法的リスクを高めているため、より強い隠蔽処理を求められたと解釈されています。Fantiaはこれを「最終防衛ライン」として自主規制強化に踏み切った形です。
2. 国際クレジットカード会社（Visa、Mastercardなど決済インフラ）
•報道やクリエイター議論で繰り返し指摘される間接的圧力。23
•背景：外資系カード会社が成人向けコンテンツを扱うプラットフォームに対し、決済停止・サービス停止の脅しをかけている（過去にFANZA、DLsite、Fantia自身などもVisa/Mastercard対応で制限を受けた事例多数）。
•影響：プラットフォームが「健全化」を進めないと決済網を失い、収益基盤が崩壊する。Fantiaも虎の穴グループとしてこの圧力を強く受け、モザイク強化で対応せざるを得なくなったとの見方が強いです。
その他の文脈
•明確な特定団体名（例：特定のNPOや政治団体）は公式・報道で出てきません。「関係諸機関」は主に警察・検察・法務省関連を指すとされています。
•決済圧力は国際的な潮流（米国のカード会社ポリシー影響）で、日本国内の二次元・同人成人コンテンツ全体に波及しています。
Fantiaはこれらを「クリエイターの安全と安定的収益環境を守るため」と位置づけていますが、クリエイター側からは「表現規制の強制」「二重包囲網」との批判も出ています。詳細はFantia公式のお知らせや関連報道で確認してください。
